For business rental or disposal of other rights under § 49(1) no. 2(f), apply its corresponding registry-only exception: where registration is the sole domestic source link, income is excluded if the parties are not related under § 1(2) AStG, or the applicable treaty, with the Act's treaty-application rules, opposes taxation. This does not exempt German land or override a different domestic source link. A property-company separator: German real-estate active book assets of EUR 40 and other active book assets of EUR 60 fail the strict more-than-50% test even if the property's market value is EUR 90. Book assets of EUR 60 and EUR 40 pass that percentage test only if the seller-attribution and relevant-time conditions also hold; the separate § 17 and treaty tests still apply.

before: Income that has had wage tax, Kapitalertragsteuer or § 50a tax withheld is settled by the withholding. No return is filed for it. Exceptions where an assessment follows:
after: For a person remaining subject to limited liability, income subject to wage tax, Kapitalertragsteuer or § 50a withholding is generally settled by that withholding. Test all the exceptions in § 50(2) sentence 2 before treating it as final:

before: - employment income where an allowance was entered in the wage tax data and pay exceeds the Grundfreibetrag plus lump sums, or where the employee applies for an assessment (EU/EEA nationals resident in the EU/EEA, and in some cases Switzerland), or in the § 46(2) nos. 2, 5 and 5a cases;
after:
- German employment income under § 49(1) no. 4 where a § 39a(4) allowance was entered and annual pay exceeds the Grundfreibetrag plus the employee and special-expense lump sums (no. 4(a)); an application under § 46(2) no. 8 (no. 4(b)); or the § 46(2) nos. 2, 5 and 5a cases (no. 4(c));
- employment applications connected with extraordinary income under § 34(1) and (2) nos. 2 and 4 (no. 4(d)), or an application for a foreign-tax credit under § 50d(7) sentence 2 (no. 4(e)); these have their own gates, rather than no. 4(b)'s nationality/residence restriction;

before: - § 50a artists, athletes and supervisory board members who apply for an assessment (EU/EEA nationals resident in the EU/EEA; assessed by the BZSt);
after: - income under § 50a(1) nos. 1, 2 and 4 on application (no. 5; assessed by the BZSt);

before: - the person is assessed as fully liable under § 1(3) or § 1a.
5. **Solidarity surcharge** at 5.5% of the income tax, with the same EUR 20,350 threshold as residents.
after: 5. **Solidarity surcharge.** Establish the assessment base under § 3 SolzG; it is not automatically the unadjusted income-tax amount. For an ordinary single assessment with no § 32d(3) or (4) tax component, it is zero when that base is at most EUR 20,350. Above that threshold, take the smaller of 5.5% of the base and 11.9% of the excess over EUR 20,350, dropping fractions of a cent (§§ 3(3), 4 SolzG). A stipulated base of EUR 20,400 gives min(EUR 1,122, EUR 5.95) = EUR 5.95. The separate § 32d(3)/(4) component and the withholding branches retain their own 5.5% treatment and do not receive this ordinary threshold/cap.

before: - Companies: treaty relief is denied to an interposed company whose owners would not get it directly and which has no real business of its own (§ 50d(3) EStG).
after: - Companies: § 50d(3) denies relief to the stated extent where both conditions hold: participating or constitutionally benefited persons would not have the entitlement if they earned the income directly, and the income source has no substantial connection with the entity's economic activity. Merely receiving or passing on the income, or activity through a business operation not adequately equipped for its purpose, is not economic activity for this test. The denial does not apply to the extent the entity proves that obtaining a tax advantage was not one of the main purposes of its interposition, or where its main class of shares is substantially and regularly traded on a recognised exchange. § 42 AO remains applicable. Lack of other economic activity alone does not displace an established statutory rebuttal; neither rebuttal nor listing creates an entitlement without the other relief conditions.

before: A foreign company that cannot use a treaty still gets two fifths of the tax back (§ 44a(9)).
after: For a capital-income creditor that is a corporation subject to limited liability within § 2 no. 1 KStG, § 44a(9) provides a refund of two fifths of the Kapitalertragsteuer actually withheld and remitted. This incorporates the application/procedure in § 50c(3) and (5) and the anti-abuse test and exceptions in § 50d(3); it is not an unconditional refund for every foreign company. Further statutory or treaty relief claims remain separate.
